summary: Initial discovery with Oryx AI exploring Redwood hosted vs dedicated vs private deployment. Customer is early-adopter startup building an automated support summarization product with PII concerns. Main asks: time-to-first-token (TTFT) for PLG flow, free credits for a pilot, latency/cost tradeoffs, security (SOC2, KMS), VPC/private deployment gating criteria. AE/SE explained free credit path, quickstart steps, and Redwood Optimize guidance (batching, quantization). Agreed next steps include sending security docs, provisioning trial credits, and scheduling technical deep dive.
topics: Security – SOC2, SSO, KMS/HSM, audit logs
Latency vs cost; quantization and batching
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Lee: hey everyone thanks for joining from Redwood, I'm Jordan, AE on this account. quick intro — we have Samira from systems and Evan our solutions eng. who do we have on the Oryx side?
[00:15] Liam Ortiz: hi this is Liam, CTO at Oryx. we also have Priya and Marcus and Nora on security. thanks for making time.
[00:27] Jordan Lee: awesome, appreciate it. the goal for today is simple — understand your constraints, time to first token expectations, and whether hosted, dedicated, or private is the right onramp. we'll cover free credits/quickstart and then map next steps.
[00:44] Priya Kumar: brief context — we're building a customer support summarization product that extracts sensitive PII and redacts it. our initial plan is a PLG flow to test with real users; we need to show low latency and keep data residency / PI controls for enterprise customers.
[01:07] Nora Finch: and security is a blocker for procurement — we need SOC2 evidence, SSO/SAML, audit logs, and KMS integration. on-prem is a future ask but for pilot we prefer hosted if encryption + access controls are good.
[01:28] Samira Patel: got it. a lot of customers start on hosted with our PLG path — we offer trial credits and a time-to-first-token playbook. typical TTFT for straightforward calls is under an hour to get a test key and run a couple of prompts, full app integration usually a few days depending on engineering availability.
[01:52] Marcus Bell: when you say "trial credits," what are the limits? and is there a way to carve out a VPC-like network or is that reserved capacity only?
[02:07] Jordan Lee: trial credits usually cover 50k–200k tokens depending on the program. we can tailor for pilot needs — we've done 100k/day pilots before. VPC/private connectivity is part of Dedicated or Private offerings; hosted doesn't expose a customer VPC, but we do provide data separation, optional dedicated capacity, and enterprise features for private control plane.
[02:34] Liam Ortiz: ok cost question up front — we care about median latency at 95th pct. We're currently targeting <350ms median for short summaries; can Redwood support that in hosted?
[02:48] Samira Patel: short answer: yes for many models under typical seq lengths. there's a tradeoff — higher perf variants or dedicated pools reduce latency and cost variance. we also recommend quantization + caching for production workloads; Redwood Optimize gives suggested config for your workload distribution.
[03:12] Priya Kumar: could you say more about caching and KV stuff? my team heard "KV cache" but not sure how it's managed.
[03:24] Samira Patel: sure, apologies the auto-transcribe often writes it as "kay-vee cache" — it's the per-session KV cache for transformers. we support prefix/KV caching server-side which reduces cost for multi-turn or repeated prefixes. it's automatic with an opt-in policy, and you control cache TTL and invalidation. that helps for repeated prompt scaffolds like system prompt plus ticket text.
[03:53] Nora Finch: security — what's your KMS story? can we use our own HSM?
[04:03] Evan Cruz: we integrate with customer-managed KMS in Dedicated and Private. Hosted uses Redwood-managed KMS but you can enable customer KMS for encryption-at-rest for enterprise plans; HSM-level integrations are available for Private on-prem installs. we'll send the security pack with exact menus.
[04:25] Marcus Bell: another practical question — we want a curl or python example to get to first call in under an hour, can we do that?
[04:34] Samira Patel: yes, the quickstart has a one-file curl and python snippet. typical flow: sign up -> get API key -> run sample prompt set -> validate outputs. we can provision a pre-funded trial account to speed that.
[04:48] Jordan Lee: i'll propose a TTFT path — 1) we send quickstart + creds today, 2) Priya runs sample prompt set and reports back latency/quality, 3) we run a 1-hour benchmark with our SE (Samira) to check token throughput and 95th pct latency.
[05:06] Priya Kumar: sounds good. about model selection — are you offering curated open models? we like to start with a smaller LLM to validate prompts, then move to a larger one.
[05:18] Samira Patel: yes — we have a model catalog with curated open models and Redwood-verified profiles. for summary tasks you'd start with a mid-sized model to tune prompts and then pick a production model. if you need very low latency we can suggest a lighter quantized variant.
[05:35] Liam Ortiz: what about dedicated capacity? if we go that route, is there a minimum commit and how fast can we spin it?
[05:44] Jordan Lee: Dedicated is reserved GPU pools. commit levels vary; typical entry is monthly reserved capacity with autoscale for bursts. spin-up time is a few hours once provisioned; for urgent pilots we can offer short-term burst access from hosted pools while dedicated is provisioned.
[06:01] Marcus Bell: procurement will ask for SOC2 report and a data flow diagram. can you share those?
[06:09] Jordan Lee: yes, that's part of the security pack Nora requested — we include SOC2, ISO summaries, SSO docs, and a data flow diagram mapping hosted vs dedicated vs private.
[06:21] Nora Finch: we need audit logs with retention controls, and a way to export logs to our SIEM.
[06:28] Evan Cruz: audit log export is supported for enterprise customers — we can stream logs to S3 or push to partner SIEMs; retention is configurable on Dedicated/Private tiers. we'll detail endpoints in the security pack.
[06:45] Priya Kumar: quick technical: what's the token pricing model during the trial? do we get per-token pricing or a flat pilot rate?
[06:54] Jordan Lee: trial credits act as prepaid token balance. for pilots we often provide a committed pilot rate for expected usage (e.g., 100k tokens/day) to make it predictable. once you decide on Dedicated or Private we draft a commit that maps to reserved capacity pricing.
[07:15] Liam Ortiz: are there examples of other early-stage companies that started hosted and then moved to dedicated? curious about friction.
[07:23] Samira Patel: frequent pattern — start hosted PLG, test via quickstart, then if you need performance predictability and VPC, migrate to Dedicated. migration is mostly configuration: model version pinning, rollout canary policies, and data plane changes. some infra work on your side but we have runbooks and an onboarding engineer to help.
[07:48] Marcus Bell: we'd like to run a baseline bench: 1) 100 concurrent short summary requests, 2) measure p50/p95 latency, 3) token throughput. can Redwood run or assist?
[08:00] Samira Patel: yes, Samira here can run bench runs and provide scripts. we can also provide a small harness that your team runs against the trial key. gives reproducible numbers.
[08:12] Priya Kumar: when you benchmark do you include warm KV cache vs cold? that affects p95.
[08:20] Evan Cruz: good call — we test both warm and cold cache; warm cache demonstrates steady-state while cold shows cold-start tails. we'll include both in the runbook.
[08:31] Jordan Lee: ok let's capture next steps: I'll send security docs + trial creds. Samira will provide bench scripts. Priya will share prompt set. we'll schedule technical deep dive with Marcus + Nora for network/security specifics.
[08:46] Liam Ortiz: timeline — we'd like to get a pilot running within the next two weeks if possible.
[08:51] Jordan Lee: feasible — we'll aim to have creds and docs to you in 48 hours, and the bench runbook within the week.
[09:00] Priya Kumar: one more thing — we may need a COLO/on-prem conversation later. for now the key is to validate the PLG funnel and prove latency and redaction quality.
[09:12] Samira Patel: totally reasonable. for redaction we have customers that run a two-step pipeline (classify/redact -> summarize) to minimize PII leakage; we can share patterns and evaluation metrics.
[09:29] Nora Finch: also, is there a contract term that locks us into a model variant that we can't change later?
[09:35] Jordan Lee: you can pin a model version for rollouts, but moving to another variant is supported; we manage migrations and fallbacks. we'll show the rollout/A-B policy in the console.
[09:49] Marcus Bell: ok thanks — this was useful. we'll look for the runbook and security pack.
[09:55] Jordan Lee: great — thanks everyone. we'll follow up with the items and get the trial provisioned. any final quick Qs?
[10:02] Liam Ortiz: none from me. thanks.
[10:05] Jordan Lee: thanks, bye.

Notes: occasional transcription errors present (e.g., "kay-vee" vs KV, product names slightly garbled). Meeting ended with explicit action items and agreed TTFT path.
